key_insight: DMA^2 shows that pixel-space diffusion distillation works better when it is adapted to RGB-specific behavior instead of copying latent-diffusion design choices. The paper finds that low-noise teacher matching is overly driven by local texture, so it shifts matching to a fixed high-noise band and adds adversarial plus anchor losses for stronger few-step generation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between modern distribution matching distillation methods and native pixel-space image generation. Existing DMD approaches are built mainly around latent diffusion and miss important characteristics of RGB space, limiting quality and efficiency in few-step generation.
method: Revisits teacher-matching for pixel-space DMD and analyzes how noise level affects what the model learns from RGB teachers.
Uses a fixed high-noise matching band to avoid overfitting to low-noise local texture cues.
Adds adversarial and anchor losses to improve realism and stabilize generation in pixel space.
impact: This work gives practitioners a better recipe for fast text-to-image generation directly in RGB space. It can improve sample quality and training stability while reducing reliance on latent-space assumptions.

paper_title: DMA$^2$: Pixel-space Distribution Matching with Adversarial and Anchor Losses
paper_authors: Xin Lin, Zhifei Zhang, Yuqian Zhou, Haitian Zheng, Shaoteng Liu
